standard_prerequisites: The flat locus closed immersion X' of the flat locus lemma of the same chapter, and base change behaviour of rig-etale and rig-surjective morphisms
The fibre product presentation of affine formal algebraic spaces over a separated base, and flatness of completed tensor products of flat algebras
The rig-smooth rig-surjectivity dichotomy for closed immersions from the same chapter
core_obligations: Base change the rig-etale rig-surjective diagonal of X along X' to obtain the same property for X' over its self product over Spf(A)
For an affine etale U over X', identify W = U x_{X'} U as a closed immersion into U x_{Spf(A)} U which is rig-etale and rig-surjective, hence an equality
Deduce that U maps injectively into Spf(A) as a map of sheaves, and extend to pairwise unions of a presentation covering to get injectivity of X' into Spf(A)
Conclude with the flatness dichotomy: X' is either empty or isomorphic to Spf(A) via a surjective cover member
proof_roadmap: Cartesianity of the square with X' and its self product, and base change of the diagonal properties
Affine local computation of W via completed tensor products and the closed immersion dichotomy
Sheaf injectivity of U to Spf(A) and its propagation to the disjoint unions of cover members
Conclude X' equals Spf(A) or is empty
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is a rigidity dichotomy: under a rig-etale rig-surjective diagonal, the flat locus X' of the chapter's flat locus lemma over the complete DVR is either empty or the whole Spf(A) (source lines 5831-5897, label lemma-flat-and-diagonal-rig-surjective). The solver must transport the diagonal property by base change, compute the self fibre product of an affine etale cover member as a completed tensor product, apply the closed immersion dichotomy for rig-smooth rig-surjective morphisms, and then promote a local sheaf injectivity to a global one via pairwise unions; the sheaf-level promotion step is the substantive part. Allowed background: the chapter's flat locus lemma and the cited formal spaces lemmas, delivered as navigation pointers.
